note: v1 90.10 (seeds 0/11 90.10/90.08), first draft of POLYMETRIC TOOL TECHNO, 'where is the one', at 132 bpm. A PHANTOM BASS made only of harmonics 2-5 of E1 (no 41 Hz energy; the ear supplies the fundamental) plays a bar that is empty on the one and hits hardest on the and-of-2, so in the break, with the kick gone, the ear takes that hit as the downbeat and the kick's return flips the phrase by an eighth. Loops of 3, 5 and 7 sixteenths (909 rim, comb-filtered Em7 stab, open-hat accents) turn against the four-on-the-floor, realigning every 105 sixteenths; a sixteen-bar build doubles the hat rate every four bars under a Shepard riser so it seems to accelerate at a fixed tempo; the kick feeds a dark reverb rumble. Form: intro 16, A 32, break 16, B 32, build 16, peak 32, outro 16 (4:53).

v2 92.03 (seeds 0/11 92.03/91.97 vs v1 re-scored now that the album has more tracks 89.17/89.16): THE BARE OUTRO and a cleaner low end. The outro now strips to the kick, the rim and the phantom bass alone - the hats leave, so the track ends on the illusion it began with - and the sections breathe further apart (intro, break and build sit 8-10 dB under the grooves). The low end was 8-10 dB over the genre and swamping the overtones the phantom fundamental is made of: the phantom bass is down 4 dB, there is a 160 Hz dip, the stab's comb moved up to 330 Hz and a 900 Hz lift fills the thin mids. Spectrum 83 -> 93, cohesion with the album 64 -> 85, and the form reads as six sections on both seeds. (Moving the rim off the 3/16 cycle to a 9/16 one broke the form, 81.7; still to solve.)
